title: Widen the unbound-source guard from html-only to every declared source type, and make offer_type Z0-reachability a measured engine-wide property
objective: Close two instances of ONE defect class: an assertion whose NAME or apparent scope covers more than its REACH. On this product that is how an unsupported free claim gets through while looking guarded.
materiality: MATERIAL. Item 1 governs whether a provider may declare an official evidence source it cannot prove; item 2 governs Z0 classification. Both are named Level-2 triggers in docs/AGENT_HARNESS.md (provider adapters and evidence extraction; Z0 classification).
autonomy_level: builder; draft PR only; does not merge; marks no feature passing
evaluation_level_rationale: Touches evidence-extraction guards and the Z0 classification engine's tests. docs/AGENT_HARNESS.md makes Level 2 mandatory for both.

The rename-to-be-honest fix the brief forbids had ALREADY been applied in a prior slice; the widening had not. The gap was documented and stationary, which is exactly the state in which a reader stops noticing it.
finding_the_brief_did_not_have.item_2: The fix the brief asks for ALREADY EXISTS: tests/unit/test_adapter_azure.py::test_offer_type_other_is_not_a_safety_mechanism, landed with the Azure slice and recorded in agent-state/progress.md line 3064. The underlying engine claim was independently re-verified and HOLDS. Rather than duplicate a shipped test, this slice fixes the SAME reach-vs-name defect in that guard: its name asserts a whole-engine property ('is not a safety mechanism') while its reach is two named frozensets, one hard-coded offer type, and one adapter's test module.

design_decisions: WIDEN, never rename-to-narrow. Answering 'does a committed capture exist?' needs no parser, so there was never a technical reason for the html-only scope -- only the accident of which walk the guard was written beside.

Two named populations instead of a filter inside one loop. DECLARED_SOURCES (all 36) serves the unbound guard; HTML_SOURCES (34) serves the grounding comparison, which genuinely needs the HTML collector. Where a walk must stay narrow, the narrowing is a population a reader can see, not a 'continue' buried in a loop.

The capture-path convention is DERIVED by inverting tests/support/fixtures.py's own maps. A second hand-written copy would be a snapshot of the day it was typed and would drift silently from the loader it mirrors.

A source type with no known capture convention FAILS LOUDLY rather than being skipped. An unmappable source would otherwise be neither confirmed bound nor reported unbound -- the exact silent-skip failure this module exists to refuse.
Set equality is retained and must not be relaxed. Pinning three known gaps is defensible ONLY because any FOURTH fails immediately. No pattern, prefix or wildcard was introduced.

Item 2 measures reachability EXHAUSTIVELY (3 x 3 x 11 x 3 x 3 x 2 = 1782 fact combinations per offer type, across 11 types) rather than probing one hand-picked best case. A probe proves one route is closed; a sweep proves every route is. eligibility and available_from are varied although the engine reads neither today, so a future gate consulting them is already covered.

Measured reachability is compared against what SELF_HOSTED_OFFER_TYPES and TEMPORARY_CONDITIONAL_OFFER_TYPES imply. That is the 'gated nowhere else' claim made executable: it fails when a gate on offer_type appears ANYWHERE outside those two frozensets.

Both hand-written parametrize lists were hoisted to named constants and reconciled against measurement rather than deleted. The typed list stays as a statement of intent; disagreement with the engine is the failure. This also means a twelfth offer type cannot be added without a test in that module classifying it.
acceptance_criteria: The unbound-source walk covers 36 of 36 declared sources, not 34.
All three pre-existing Cloudflare gaps are pinned under set equality; a FOURTH unbound source of ANY type fails immediately, including a non-html one.
No guard was weakened, and no pattern/wildcard/subset check was introduced, to make anything pass.
offer_type=other's Z0 reachability is an executed, measured property whose failure message says the engine became SAFER if it ever changes.
Every guard is two-sided: shown to REFUSE what it must AND to PERMIT a legitimately-free offer.
Every mutation of the SUBJECT is killed by a NAMED test, and both no-op negative controls stay green.
Zero diff on PR #95's paths and on every forbidden path.

negative_and_regression_tests.method: Mutation, not coverage. Each mutation edits the SUBJECT (provider config, fixture bytes, or the engine) and requires a NAMED test to go red. Predictions were recorded in writing BEFORE execution, including the arms expected to pass. Originals restored via raw bytes; a post-restore run verifies green.
negative_and_regression_tests.notable: M8 (removing 'trial' from TEMPORARY_CONDITIONAL_OFFER_TYPES) was predicted UNCERTAIN before running and did NOT fail the refuse-arm test, because that test iterates the same frozenset it checks -- both sides move together. It was caught instead by the reconciliation test and by test_z2_for_temporary_conditional_offer_types. The uncertain prediction was recorded in advance precisely so this could not be retrofitted.
